basis: Debates 1–226 reuse the corrected September 1 position taxonomy. Later entries below classify the published proposition and side labels, not personal religious identity. null excludes comparisons that do not oppose a religious claim to a skeptical or secular alternative.

exclusionReasons.229: Historical existence of Jesus is not itself a theistic claim.
exclusionReasons.230: Idealism versus naturalism does not establish a theism-versus-skepticism comparison.
exclusionReasons.231: A soul claim is not itself a claim about God's existence.
exclusionReasons.234: Two accounts of consciousness and purpose; no clear opposing religious and skeptical positions.
exclusionReasons.235: A nonphysical soul is not itself a claim about God's existence.
exclusionReasons.236: Moral realism versus anti-realism does not separate theism from skepticism.
exclusionReasons.240: Alternative accounts of cosmic purpose and divinity.
exclusionReasons.246: Alternative models of God; rejection of simplicity need not challenge theism.
exclusionReasons.248: Dispute over classical-theist explanations rather than an unambiguous theism-versus-skepticism pair.
exclusionReasons.254: Team-debate approximation is excluded from this one-on-one comparison.
exclusionReasons.264: Spiritual nondualism cannot safely be equated with theism.
exclusionReasons.294: Both speakers argue within religious commitments; disagreement about conquest is not a theism-versus-skepticism pair.
